items.description: The Kalahari Basin is a vast, sandy interior region characterizing a significant part of the northern interior plateau.
The Karoo consists of broad basins and ranges, forming a major part of the central interior of South Africa.
The Limpopo Plains are characterized by lower-lying, flat topographical features in the northern part of the country.
The Lowveld is a region of gentle slopes and plains east of the Drakensberg mountains, extending toward the coast.
The Namib fringe area features transitional topography between the interior plateau and the western coastal plains.
The Suurberg is a prominent mountain range contributing to the diverse relief of the Eastern Cape province.
Winterberg is a mountainous area forming part of the rugged high-relief landscape in the Eastern Cape.
The Amathole Mountains offer a dramatic, forested high-relief landscape in the Eastern Cape region.
The Waterberg is a vast sandstone plateau and mountainous area located in the Limpopo province.
The Kharras region contributes to the complex, elevated terrain that defines parts of the interior plateau.
Komsberg is an elevated region characterized by rugged mountain passes and high plateau relief.
The Rooge region forms a distinct part of the intricate, multi-layered topographical landscape of the interior.
The Kogelberg mountain range provides dramatic, high-altitude relief and rugged peaks near the coast.
Blouberg is a distinctive mountain range featuring notable elevation and complex, rugged topography.
